Note that the core number excluded a Bt1. 52bn (pre-tax) gain on the fair value of investment properties. Core earning was in line with our estimate and the consensus. Result highlights 1Q26 revenue totaled Bt 5.2bn, up by 12% YoY and 5% QoQ. Hotel & services income was Bt 4.1bn, up 13% YoY and 10% QoQ. The YoY increase was due to improved hotel performance for its MICE hotels, luxury resorts, as well as additional revenue from newly opened hotels. Commercial space revenue was Bt 1.13m for 1Q26, up by 16% YoY but down by 5% QoQ. The YoY increase was due to the new Jurassic World: The Experience project at its Asiatique property. Outlook We expect AWC’s 2Q26 earnings to grow slightly YoY, driven mainly by hotels opened in 2025 and higher revenue contribution from the Asiatique project. However, we expect 2Q26 earnings to drop QoQ, due to Thailand’s tourism low season. What’s changed? We maintain our forecast numbers. Recommendation We believe AWC’s share price fully reflect s its growth narrative, with valuation now discounting much of the near -term earnings upside. At 3 4x 2026 PER — well above its peers — risk-reward has turned less compelling. With limited catalysts in the near term and upside to our target price capped, we maintain our HOLD recommendation on fundamentals and view AWC as another tourism stock for tactical trim- weight positioning.
